b.title: Expose GitHub search quotas and MCP 429 retry hints
b.body:
GitHub MCP `search_code` can exhaust its smaller search budget while `core` quota remains available. Missing bucket snapshots and buried 429 retry hints make these failures difficult to diagnose.

- **Quota visibility:** Log `core`, `code_search`, and `search` limit, remaining, and reset values before and after agent execution, using GitHub tools credential precedence. End snapshots run on failure; logging remains nonfatal.
- **429 diagnostics:** Surface failed MCP responses and server retry hints across gateway/RPC logs, including legacy summaries. Exclude queries and URLs; avoid interpreting echoed queries or `Retry-After` values as HTTP statuses.
- **Documented alternative:** Explain search budgets and recommend authenticated cross-repository `checkout:` with `sparse-checkout` for local code searches.

Example summary entry:

```text
github | search_code | try again in 216.007769ms
```

- Fixes #68666

`gh aw audit` could report failed sub-agents as successful, disagree on aliased or dated model IDs, and omit per-agent usage and cost. This change adds structured sub-agent outcomes, shared model identity resolution, and per-agent attribution across audit and logs reports.

- **Outcomes and findings:** Track completed, failed, and incomplete invocations, effort, and sanitized errors. Failed invocations without served requests no longer receive an effective model; audit reports a “Sub-agent Failed” finding.
- **Model identity:** Resolve aliases, provider-qualified patterns, Anthropic version spellings, and dated IDs consistently. Parse pi dispatch, usage, and terminal-result events instead of relying on `agent-stdio.log` when structured events are available.
- **Usage and cost:** Include per-agent requests, tokens, credits, models, effort, and outcomes. Attribute pi credits by matching proxy entries on model, token tuple, and time order; warn on unmatched usage or endpoint-specific credit differences. Preserve existing routing cost buckets while adding main-agent and per-sub-agent splits.
- **Reports and schemas:** Carry the breakdown through audit, logs, cross-run summaries, comparisons, console rendering, and the audit/logs JSON schemas.

Example attribution:

{

  "resolved_model": "gpt-5.4-mini",
  "served_models": ["gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17"],

b.title: refactor(tools): stop re-exporting extract_first_matching_tool from the tools package
b.body:
## Description

The tools services package (`gateway.services.tools`) still exports `extract_first_matching_tool` from its package root, but nothing outside the package uses it. Moving web tool admission into the tools services (1d8f2903) added the export so that `routes/_tools.py` could call the helper. Moving code execution admission there as well (793226aa) removed that last caller. Now only the package's own private modules call the helper, and they import it from `_declarations` directly. This PR removes the root re-export and its `__all__` entry. The function itself stays.

Nothing changes for anyone using Otari.

**This removes a public name, so a human must review it before it merges.** I searched this repository (source, tests, scripts, docs and the dashboard) and found no other use. A consumer outside this repository, such as the `otari-ai` enterprise overlay, could still import `extract_first_matching_tool` from `gateway.services.tools`, and a search here cannot rule that out. The risk is low: before this window the helper was the private `_extract_first_matching_tool` in `routes/_tools.py`, and the public export has existed for about a day. Please check the overlay before merging. If it imports the name, close this PR.

## How to test it locally

- `make lint-python`: every hook passed (architecture check, Alembic single head, ruff check, ruff format).
- `make typecheck-python`: mypy reported no issues in 947 source files.
- `uv run pytest -q -n auto tests/unit`:

`gh aw audit` could report failed sub-agents as successful, disagree on aliased or dated model IDs, and omit per-agent usage and cost. This change adds structured sub-agent outcomes, shared model identity resolution, and per-agent attribution across audit and logs reports.
